blocks.text: ETOBICOKE'S POSTWAR-TO-MODERN DEMOLITION
★★★★★ 700+ Five-Star Reviews on Google
Demolition That Reads a Backyard's Age Before Touching Anything

c: Etobicoke’s housing tells one story on repeat — solid postwar bungalows meeting owners ready to finally update everything about them, including the backyard. In Alderwood, Mimico and Long Branch, that usually means an original above ground pool, an aging deck or a shed that’s been there since the house was built, torn down as part of a bigger renovation the family’s been planning for years. Around Islington City Centre and the Kingsway’s larger properties, it’s bigger structures on bigger lots, handled with the same attention paid to anything else on an established property. Along the Lake Shore strips, it’s the occasional commercial patio or fence coming down between tenants. And through Rexdale and the newer streets further north, it’s the more straightforward version of the job — a fence or a garage cleared ahead of a project that’s already underway. The 700+ five-star reviews behind Live Junk Free consistently mention the same thing: a crew that knew the difference between a fifty-year-old structure and a five-year-old one, and handled each accordingly.

blocks.text: DEMOLITION FAQ
Demolition Services in Etobicoke — Postwar Questions, Modern Answers

items.q: How much does demolition cost in Etobicoke?
a: It depends on the structure, not its age — a fence section is inexpensive, a full above ground pool or a concrete patio costs more given the crew time involved. The figure is confirmed free at the walkthrough and holds to the invoice.

items.q: Our pool and deck are original to a fifties bungalow — does that change anything?
a: It changes the approach, not the price. Older installations sometimes have corroded fasteners, buried footings or hidden wear, and the crew accounts for that at the walkthrough rather than discovering it mid-job.

items.q: Can you handle demolition on a larger Kingsway or estate-pocket property?
a: Yes — bigger lots and structures are regular work for us, with the same standard of grounds and driveway protection applied whatever the scale.

items.q: What's involved in concrete or flooring demolition?
a: The patio, walkway or driveway gets broken up with equipment matched to its thickness, then hauled off in manageable pieces. The site is left level and cleared.

items.q: Can demolition happen the same day I call?
a: Often, yes. Trucks run Etobicoke daily, 6AM to 11PM, seven days a week — a morning call frequently becomes an afternoon demolition.
